changed.title: Known result rebuilt. Exact routing length for invertible binary affine maps with cyclic feedback
changed.statement:
∀ (b L : ℕ),
  let w := b + 1
  let V := Fin w → ZMod 2
  (∀ (g : V ≃ₗ[ZMod 2] V) (v : V),
    ∃ (tap : Fin L → Fin b → ZMod 2) (bias : Fin L → ZMod 2),
      ∀ x : V, (List.finRange L).foldl (fun (s : V) i =>
        let tail := fun j : Fin b => s j.succ
        Fin.snoc (α := fun _ : Fin w => ZMod 2) tail
          (s 0 + bias i + ∑ j : Fin b, tap i j * tail j)) x = g x + v) ↔
    2 * w - 1 ≤ L
changed.unlocks: determines the exact physical length needed for a binary shift register to realize all invertible affine maps
changed.context: Build a suffix flag complementary to both the input and target coordinate prefix flags. At each extension avoid the union of two proper hyperplanes. Choose its basis adapted to the input prefix flag. The initial forward sweep writes this triangular basis, leaving the initial bit unchanged. A second sweep writes the targets since each mixed list is a basis. Absorb biases and omit the initial fixed rotation by retargeting. At 2w-2 steps the last two logical cells have one visit each. Swapping them would duplicate an untouched bit. For w=1 use the flip.

changed.title: A joint encoding of many translated-list choices still forces high degree for every nonzero parity of fixed answers
changed.statement:
∀ (g a : Nat), 0 < g → 0 < a →
  let M := 2^a
  let m := M-1
  let d := g*a
  let V := Fin g × Fin m × Fin a
  let W := V → Bool
  let deg := fun (b : Nat) (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ b) ∧
      ∀ input, f input = (((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, input j = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let Y := Fin g → Fin M
  let valid := fun (x : W) (choice : Y) =>
    ∀ j i, ∃ v : Fin a, x (j,i,v) ≠ (choice j).val.testBit v.val
  let run := fun (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (x : W) =>
    (List.range d).foldl (fun h pos => h + ((ask pos h x).toNat <<< pos)) 0
  (∃ (choose : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (decode : Nat → Y),
    (∀ (u : Fin d) (h : Nat),
      deg ((u.val%a+1)*2^(a-1-u.val%a)) (choose u.val h)) ∧
    ∀ input, valid input (decode (run choose input))) ∧
  (∀ (n : Nat) (choose : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (decode : Nat → Y),
    (∀ input, valid input (decode ((List.range n).foldl (fun trace tick =>
      trace + ((choose tick trace input).toNat <<< tick)) 0))) → d ≤ n) ∧
  ∀ (ask : Fin d → W → Bool) (report : (Fin d → Bool) → Y)
    (label : Fin g → Fin m → Fin M → Fin a → Bool),
    (∀ x j i, (fun rawBit => x (j,i,rawBit)) ≠ label j i (report (fun u => ask u x) j)) →
    ∀ (mask : Finset (Fin d)), mask.Nonempty → ∀ b : Nat,
      deg b (fun word => (((mask.filter (fun bitId => ask bitId word = true)).card % 2) == 1)) →
      2^(a-1) ≤ b
changed.unlocks: Separates the total degree of a minimum-length fixed batch from the adaptive selector on many groups.
changed.context: Concatenate the absent-prefix selectors. Every tuple of labels can be forced by independent inputs in the groups, so shorter transcripts cannot suffice. At exact length ga the report on all transcripts is bijective. A nonempty parity becomes a nonconstant test on the tuple of labels. Connect opposite-valued tuples by changing one label at a time. Some line has both values. The cut restriction on that line has at least 2^(a-1) independent OR variables.
